correctness.rationale: Closed-form logistic stage flow and accumulated catch yield exact rational and logarithmic formulas. The difference of terminal stocks has strictly positive sign because n-m=(H-L)pq>0. For two strictly positive efforts, strict monotonicity of the quotient A/B follows from factorized A'/B' and the inequality 1+q(1-L)>0; its limits force precisely one root. Weighted Jensen strictly places it above z=1, and L=0 yields exactly z=1. Edge cases H or L equal to or above one use integral J definitions, avoiding apparent 0/0. Standalone 2000 reproducible numerical checks passed but are not used as proof.

originality.rationale: Targeted full-text and semantic comparison found no implication covering the full finite-horizon two-positive-effort crossover theorem. Yu--Tang--Lou derive classical flow and a periodic-attractor annual-yield optimization, not fixed-initial-biomass two-positive-effort reordering with a unique threshold above K; Córdova-Lepe et al. address instantaneous catch impulses and variable closed seasons. Stronger general-control coverage remains a documented unresolved literature risk but no decisive equivalent surfaced.
residual_risks: A stronger unlocated optimal-harvesting or control-theoretic flow-interchange result may imply the two-rate initial-stock crossover without matching its terminology.

The degenerate closed-season case is an algebraic consequence of known Riccati flow formulas, so originality is based on the simultaneous positive-rate global uniqueness, threshold location and stock/catch conflict, not on that case alone.
Semantic literature search is not a proof of uniqueness in the literature.

value.rationale: The unique initial-biomass crossover answers a natural fishery-management comparison between fixed high/low seasonal effort orders and exposes a sharp catch-vs-terminal-stock conflict across all positive durations. The exact carrying-capacity boundary for closure and the strict super-capacity shift with positive baseline fishing give a biologically meaningful, independently motivated classification; it is not a fitted constant, mere rescaling, or narrow arbitrary benchmark. The theorem is limited to deterministic logistic fisheries and is not claimed optimal among all schedules.
